payload.rationale: This document is a sprint retro that directly echoes the prior Sprint 4 retro (Sample_Sprint4Retro_20260322): same async decision widget, same 23-point velocity claim, same Zephyr-as-key-unlock attribution. I expanded every position and observation from that prior retro so the passes can bind this document to existing records rather than minting duplicates — including Position_ZephyrIntegrationUnlock, Obs_TinaVelocity, Position_Sprint4ThesisProven, and Obs_ZephyrRateLimitResolved. I also expanded the Narrative_AntiSlackPositioning subtree (AntiPatternRealtimeChat, ProductCategoryAsyncPlatform, TargetMarketRemoteTeams) because the widget is the product instantiation of that positioning thesis, and the pricing positions (PricingTier25Plus, PricingTwelveDollars) because they were decided in the same prior sprint retro and this document may extend or confirm them. No areas were deliberately excluded — the document is short but each clause maps to a load-bearing prior position.

^-marked entries are compressed stubs carrying child addresses. Their narration and any surfaced witness quotes are verbatim-accurate — quote them as-is — but a stub carries no provenance (source, date, supersession). Expand (aswritten_expand with the IRIs you need) before any claim that turns on WHEN or by WHOM something was said, or whether it is still the current framing. Witness-depth sections below already carry full provenance.

Deciding where to go: each mapped area's narration tells you the SPAN of what lives under it; the area index names everything else. Expand a subtree when its narration (or name) shows your subject plausibly lives there — you'll get the trajectory, the variants, and the verbatim witness. But be strict about absence: if neither the map's narrations nor the index's names substantively cover your subject, it is NOT in this perspective — say so rather than expanding a loose thematic match (a word-overlap is not coverage). Decide from the map; expand to ground.

positions.name: SprintDeliveryAccounting
positions.frame: how does the team account for a sprint's outcomes — what shipped, how it measured, and what drove it?
positions.why: All three expressions share a matter-of-fact, past-tense, informational register: they recount settled facts about Sprint 4 without hedging or performance. src-1 declares the deliverable, src-2 supplies the velocity metric as evidence, and src-3 attributes the outcome to a single causal factor. Together they form a retrospective accounting — the team reporting what happened, measured how, and why it worked — read through a shared stance of composed, communal pride.

placements.why: The async decision widget is the product embodiment of the decision-capture-at-consensus thesis. Shipping it (src-1), reporting the velocity that delivered it (src-2), and identifying the Zephyr integration that enabled cross-platform capture (src-3) are all evidence that the narrative is being operationalized as a shipped product. These are position-grain facts (a sprint's delivery accounting) that support the existing thematic leaf rather than naming a new theme.
